newsitem.title: USA: Cellular Technical says can meet forecast.
newsitem.headline: Cellular Technical says can meet forecast.

text.p: Cellular Technical Services Co on Thursday said it is comfortable it can meet financial analysts' first quarter earnings estimates.

"Based on our expectations for revenue recognition in the first three months of the year...we are comfortable with current analyst earnings estimates for the first quarter," Stephen Katz, chief executive officer, said in a statement.
The company, however, did not say what analysts' first quarter forecasts, are and a spokesman was unavailable to comment.

Cellular Technical Services Company Inc, a provider of real-time information management systems for the wireless communications industry, said it expects to recognize more than $17 million in revenue from its Blackbird Platform and PreTect fraud prevention system.
Also, the company's first quarter revenue expectation includes over $7 million of deferred revenue associated with about 300 cell site units deployed in 1996's fourth quarter.
The first quarter also assumes increased expenses mainly for sales and marketing as well as research and development.
For the full-year 1997, the company expects to recognize revenue on about 3,000 cell site units.

"In terms of the number of cell site units we expect to deploy on a quarterly basis, we anticipate the strongest growth will take place in the second half of the year," Katz said. "Thus, while quarterly results may vary, we believe total revenue and earnings per share for 1997 will be in line with the current range of analyst estimates."
Analysts expect the company to report a profit of $0.77 a share for the 1997 year based on a range of estimates between $0.70 and $0.84 a share, according to investment research firm First Call.
Finally, Katz said he has assumed day-to-day direction of the company's operations.
"The company is at a key turning point in its development and is poised to achieve significant growth through 1997 and beyond," Katz said.
